components.name: Button
components.usage: Use for actions; use asChild with a link for navigation. Use `loading` (not `disabled` plus a hand-placed spinner) while an action is in flight: it keeps full color, shows a spinner, sets aria-busy, and blocks clicks. components.name: Avatar
components.usage: Use for a person or account image with a fallback. Pick `size` (sm/default/lg) and a fallback `tone` (secondary/primary/accent/muted) instead of custom classes; pair AvatarImage with AvatarFallback initials. Accessibility: Use meaningful image alt text unless the adjacent text already names the person. Label initials when they are the only identification; avoid redundant announcements. AvatarImage needs a meaningful alt (the person's name), or alt="" when the name is already shown next to it.

</Avatar>

components.usage: Use for focused tasks that require a modal. Use AlertDialog, not Dialog, to confirm deletion or other irreversible actions. examples.code:

  <DialogTrigger asChild><Button type="button">Edit reflection</Button></DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent>
    <DialogHeader><DialogTitle>Edit your question</DialogTitle>
      <DialogDescription>Make room for another perspective before continuing.</DialogDescription></DialogHeader>
    <DialogFooter><DialogClose asChild><Button variant="outline">Keep draft</Button></DialogClose></DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>

components.name: StatusBadge
components.usage: Use to show a transaction's lifecycle state (pending, processing, completed, failed, refunded, cancelled, on-hold). Cancelled is muted without strikethrough; On hold is outlined coral so it is not confused with Failed. Accessibility: Every status renders an icon plus a text label, so meaning never relies on color alone. Icons are aria-hidden; override the text with label when a more specific reason helps (e.g. "Card declined").

components.name: ApprovalCard
components.usage: Use for any approve/reject decision on a payout, refund, or expense. The parent owns state and persistence. Accessibility: Reject requires a written reason by default and confirms in an AlertDialog whose focus starts on "Keep pending". Busy state sets aria-busy and disables both actions; the label changes to "Saving".

examples.label: Approval Card

antipatterns: Let approvals happen with a single click and no confirmation for rejections.

components.name: AgentActionCard
components.usage: Use when a person must review an action an AI agent proposes. Shows the action (with its stable actionId and proposedAt time), parameters, policy checks, and rationale. Failed checks block Approve unless the reviewer overrides with a written reason; flagged checks need an acknowledgment. Each decision is logged to the built-in ActivityTimeline with a UUID, the actionId, and the app-supplied actor.id; persist it via onDecision. Times are shown in each visitor's own time zone after load, with the exact instant always in the time element's dateTime attribute. Accessibility: Policy checks show an icon plus a Passed/Flagged/Failed word, never color alone. The override and acknowledgment controls are labeled checkboxes; the override reason is a labeled, required textarea. Approve stays a disabled native button until the gate is satisfied; Reject keeps its reason + AlertDialog confirmation. Every timestamp is a real <time dateTime> instant; the visible label is the visitor's own time zone and appears after load.

examples.label: Agent refund review

antipatterns: Pass a free-form reviewer name instead of the real actor ID, generate IDs from list length, or hide failed/flagged checks.
Render your own clock- or locale-dependent timestamp string instead of passing the ISO instant and letting the card label it.
